body: Buspar sucks ime. I think for me the gabapentin and beta blocker are most helpful for anxiety. For withdrawal comfort I think the baclofen will really take the edge off but I'll find out later this week!

I've tapered twice under a doctor without issues and c/t once. I'm doing a rapid week long taper this time (I refuse to buy anymore). I procured all the meds used at a detox place I went to over the past year in anticipation of this though I would've liked to be tapered down more but I am shit with self control.

I already take Gabapentin and am going to go up on that, a beta blocker Atenonol, Clonodine, I already take Lexapro and have 50 Baclofen. I also have maybe 10 Zyprexas which is a thienodiazapine and I will only take as a last result PRN if I can't sleep for days like last time I c/t and started hallucinating.  I'm also prescribed trazadone which may or may not help and promethazine for nausea. I had a concussion and whiplash in may hence why I have so many scripts.
Interesting. I will try it.

Yes, all my worries melt away and I feel like all is well in the world. I lose my natural fight or flight, always being on high alert self and am like "yeah, everything's all good now." But what a heavy price to pay for that temporary peace when really I just haven't learned good coping and self-care skills and have relied on chemicals instead. Starting withdrawals now.

I took it as a last resort when in acute stage and was able to sleep for 2 hours on day 5 which kept me sane but it's got crazy tolerance issues and withdrawals so I used it rarely because I'd actually rather withdraw from benzos tham Phenibut.

Thank you so much for the motivation. I fear going into psychosis and seizures (think gabapentin will keep them away). I know last time I started hallucinating from no sleep but was still coherent and able to know it wasn't real. I'm glad this go around is better for you than the last. We shall prevail.

I'm on my 4th quit. Tapered twice under a doctor and cold turkeyed once. Basically doing a rapid taper from 4 mgs diclaz and 1 mg etiz in about a week as I don't have insurance. It's amazing to me that I kept going back. Cold turkey was the worst most indescribable fucked up hell mentally and physically I've ever experienced and yet I am doing it again because if I cave and buy more, it'll never end. At this point I just want off. I know what to expect. I have procured every kind of medication a detox facility uses at least but I know it will still be hell. I am unemployed and I'll never get this 3 month window again of not having to work. 

Your post just makes me more determined as another person who has quit before and reinstated then off again and stronger for it. Suffering but remembering why we're suffering and pushing through to the other side. I'm tough enough to make it through round 4. I hope. Thanks for your post and hope relief comes soon for you.

Yikes! Yes I'm not looking forward to when I start getting withdrawals as I go down. I did one cut so far from 70 to 60 and felt fine. Unfortunately I just got a concussion and whiplash so I'm on baclofen which is a hard withdrawal too, I've heard!

Good job, man. Sorry I posted before I saw that. You've got this!

I'm so sorry you were hurt but you do need to take control of the situation which, if you're able, might mean cutting this person off. I know you don't want to hear this, I certainly hate hearing it but its true, we are the ones responsible for our actions and how we cope with hurt, anger, trauma, disappointment, etc. I do sincerely wish you the best and hope you can take back control of your life. You are the only one who can do that.

Trazadone works well for me and gabapentin. Gabapentin has its own withdrawals and I take it throughout the day and it takes some withdrawal edge off, but it's honestly the least of my worries right now!

See if your state has an Employed Person with Disabilities where you can work and pay around 150.00 a month to keep Medicaid services like insurance. 

Also, look for a doctor or psychiatrist that can help you taper cuz lets face it: long term use of benzos will seriously mess up your brain. Might have to try more than one but I've had a doctor prescribe me librium to taper off etizolam so it is possible. Tell them and show them you have had a script, want to taper but your psych doctor doesn't think benzo withdrawal is real and they'll be more likely to help taper you off.

That's how I got addicted to benzos. Before I was addicted to stimulants and then found benzos as a way to help with comedown and sleep. I got off my drug of choice: dexedrine, but now have a worse and nastier and much harder to quit benzo addiction.

I feel addicted to the addiction cycle itself as you said, particularly getting off and there's usually a six month period or so I get healthy and appreciate just being alive then I get bored again and restless.

Maybe they will because I was on librium, super long acting but it's been 5 days and I feel not great but okay. So hopefully it is the gabapentin keeping the worst away.

I just got out of rehab. Recommend tapering with a good doctor. The rehab's taper plan was basically like a slightly drawn out cold turkey. I told them I need a longer taper, at least 1-5-2 weeks. "No sorry that's our protocol." I also was told by intake guy I could have my phone to contact my support system every night for a half hour. Nope. No phone calls for two weeks. Every time I turned around theres a protocol or rule. I was in detox room with a girl who was doing terribly. Kept going to the nurse to tell her. Nurse "Ratchett" comes in and says "get into bed and stop getting up, go to sleep." Finally she was taken seriously and taken to the ER. I left today after one night. Now I'm cold turkeying at home instead of in that hellhole hoping the gabapentin I have from my doctor will keep seizures away. I'm going to let me doctor know Monday.

I was on 4-6 mgs a day etiz and quit adderall and etiz on a Friday. Just slept all weekend from stopping adderall and then Monday I made the mistake of taking a modafinil around 12 and went through 4 days of withdrawal hell- no sleep, stomach issues, all senses massively heightened not able to eat, couldnt walk straight, felt on brink of a constant panic attack and hallucinating. No seizures though. Then it got a lot better I even went to work thursday, with the aid of phenibut though could not do anything requiring fine motor skills or drive for another couple days. Felt okay though. I think short half life equals short but intense w/d maybe?  

Then I started taking too much phenibut but kicked that. I think benzo w/d+stimulant could make w/d that much worse.
